forecast-period.text: A trough of low pressure lies north of the South Australian border over the Northern Territory. A high pressure system moves across waters to the south of the state reaching the Tasman Sea later on Thursday. Another trough of low pressure moves into the far west on Friday before weakening over the weekend.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Showers and isolated thunderstorms about the pastoral districts, easing during the evening. Otherwise dry apart from the light morning showers about southern coasts. Maximum temperatures below to well below average. East to southeasterly winds, fresh at times about the west coast and in the northeast.

Dry at first. Isolated showers and possible thunderstorms developing in the far west during the afternoon and evening. Maximum temperatures near average about western coasts, grading to below average in the northeast. Southeast to northeasterly winds.

Showers and thunderstorms in the west, contracting to the far north during the afternoon and evening. Maximum temperatures near to above average about coastal districts, grading to below average about the pastoral districts. East to northeasterly winds, with local afternoon sea breezes

text.p: Showers and possible thunderstorms developing in the west. Possible showers near the eastern border. Maximum temperatures near to above average about the south and west, grading to below average in the northeast. East to northeasterly winds, with local afternoon sea breezes.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Saturday: Broadly 5 to 10 mm across the pastoral districts, increasing 10 to 20 mm in the northwest with isolated falls of 20 to 40 mm. Less than 2 mm across the southeast.
